reflection_question: What are you building right now, and what is the one defence you most need around it?
devotional_text:
There is a book in the Old Testament about a man rebuilding a wall around a ruined city, and it is one of the most useful books in Scripture for somebody in recovery.

Nehemiah is not a story about avoiding trouble. It is a story about building while under attack.

# The Situation

Jerusalem's walls are rubble. Nehemiah comes back to rebuild them, and the moment the work starts, the opposition starts.

First mockery — *what are these feeble people doing, will they finish in a day?*

Then threats. Then a plan to attack.

And this is the detail that matters: **the opposition arrived because the building started.**

It was not there when the walls were rubble. Nobody attacks a ruin. They attack a construction site.

If things have got harder since you started this study, that is not a sign you are doing it wrong.

## What Nehemiah Does

> "But we made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against them day and night, because of them." (Nehemiah 4:9)

Read both halves, because almost everybody is better at one than the other.

**They prayed.** And **they set a watch.**

Not prayer instead of a guard. Not a guard instead of prayer. Both, in one sentence, with no sense of contradiction.

Some people in this fight pray and take no practical precautions at all, and call that faith. Others build elaborate systems and never pray, and wonder why they are exhausted.

Nehemiah did both and thought nothing of it.

## The Picture That Sticks

> "Those who built the wall, and those who bore burdens loaded themselves; everyone with one of his hands did the work, and with the other held his weapon." (Nehemiah 4:17)

> "Among the builders, everyone wore his sword at his side, and so built." (Nehemiah 4:18)

A trowel in one hand and a sword at the side.

**Building and defending at the same time**, because waiting for the threat to pass before starting the wall means the wall never gets built.

That is your life for the next while. You do not get to recover first and then live. You build the new thing while still fighting the old one. Both hands occupied, every day.

## Something Else He Did

> "I looked, and rose up, and said to the nobles, to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, 'Don't be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.'" (Nehemiah 4:14)

He stationed families together, by household, at the most exposed parts of the wall.

He made it personal. *Fight for your sons and your daughters and your houses.*

Abstract motivation collapses at 11 p.m. Specific people do not.

And he put a trumpeter beside himself: wherever you hear the trumpet, **come to us there.** A way of calling for help that everybody agreed on in advance.

That is Day 9's door and Day 28's person, three thousand years early.

## The Wall Got Built

It took fifty-two days. Not fifty-two days of peace — fifty-two days of carrying a sword.

And at the end there was a wall.

## What To Watch For In Nehemiah 4

* 😏 The mockery in verses 2 and 3, and what it is aimed at
* 🙏 The two halves of verse 9
* 😩 Verse 10, where the builders themselves say the strength is failing — honest exhaustion mid-project
* 👨‍👩‍👧 Who Nehemiah tells them to fight for, in verse 14
* 🛠️ The trowel and the sword in verses 17 and 18
* 📯 The trumpet in verses 19 and 20 — an agreed signal for help

## The Bigger Takeaway

You are not going to get a quiet period in which to rebuild your life.

The pressure went up when you started, and it will stay up for a while. That is what happens on a building site.

**Pray and set a watch. Build with one hand and keep the other on the sword. And agree, in advance, on the signal you will use when you need help.**

## Today's One Thing

**Set your watch, and agree your trumpet.**

Two parts, both practical.

**The watch** — one defence you have not yet put in place. The filter, the password somebody else holds, the money moved, the route changed, the app that reports to another person. One, today.

**The trumpet** — an agreed signal with the person from Day 28. A single word by text that means *it is bad right now*, so you do not have to compose a paragraph in your worst hour.

Agree it with them today. Something simple. One word.

Then you have a wall going up, a sword at your side, and a way to call for help.

## Today's Prayer

God,

It has got harder since I started, and I was taking that as a sign I was failing.

Nehemiah's wall was attacked because it was being built. Nobody bothers with rubble.

So help me build anyway. With one hand if that is all I have free.

Teach me to pray and set a watch — not one or the other, both, without thinking one is less spiritual than the other.

Remind me who I am fighting for when the motivation runs out at the end of a long day.

And when I sound the trumpet, send somebody.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: What are you carrying today that actually belongs to next month?
devotional_text:
One of the heaviest things a person in this fight carries is the future.

Not today. Today is usually survivable.

It is the weight of *always*. Never again, for the rest of my life. Every Christmas, every holiday, every bad night, forever, without it.

That is not a load anybody can lift, and you have been trying to lift it every morning.

# The Prayer Jesus Taught

In the middle of the Lord's Prayer there is a line most people say without hearing.

> "Give us today our daily bread." (Matthew 6:11)

**Today. Daily.**

Not a storehouse. Not next month's supply. Today's.

The word used there carries the sense of bread sufficient for the day. It is the same arrangement as the manna in the wilderness, where Israel gathered enough for one day and anything hoarded went bad overnight.

God has always worked this way with His people, and it frustrates everybody, because we would all prefer the storehouse.

## Why He Does It This Way

A storehouse would let you stop coming.

Daily bread means a daily conversation. That is not a flaw in the system; it is the point of it.

And for you specifically, it means something else: **you are not expected to have next year's strength today.**

You will not be given the grace for a Christmas in eight months' time. Not now. You will be given it in eight months, on the day.

## Then He Says It Plainly

> "Therefore don't be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day's own evil is sufficient." (Matthew 6:34)

**Each day's own evil is sufficient.**

Today has enough in it. Do not import more.

That is not a platitude. It is a load management instruction, and it is the same thing Moses said on Day 30 with the word *today*.

## What This Looks Like When It Is Bad

When it is really bad, the unit gets smaller, and that is allowed.

* 📅 Today
* 🕐 This afternoon
* ⏳ The next hour
* ⏱️ The next ten minutes
* 🫁 This breath

People have got through the worst nights of their lives in ten minute units. There is no prize for using a larger one.

If "today" is too big right now, use "until 4 p.m." That is not weakness. That is sizing the load to what you can actually lift.

## The Part About Birds

The passage around it is about anxiety — food, clothes, tomorrow.

> "See the birds of the sky, that they don't sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you of much more value than they?" (Matthew 6:26)

And then:

> "Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?" (Matthew 6:27)

That is the question to put against the forever-weight.

All that worrying about whether you will still be clean in five years — what has it produced? Has a single hour of it helped? Or has it mostly just made today harder, and made the thing more attractive as a way of escaping the dread?

**Anxiety about the future is one of the most reliable triggers there is.** It is not just unpleasant. It is dangerous for you specifically.

## What To Watch For In Matthew 6:25-34

* 🐦 The birds in verse 26, and what He says they do not do
* ⏱️ The question in verse 27 about what worry adds
* 🌸 The lilies, and that even Solomon was not dressed like one
* 🥇 "Seek first God's Kingdom" in verse 33 — the reordering
* 📆 The instruction in verse 34, and the reason given

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been trying to carry your whole future sobriety on a Tuesday morning, and it is crushing you.

You were never asked to.

**Today's bread for today. Tomorrow has its own, and it will be there when tomorrow is.**

## Today's One Thing

**Put down what is not today's.**

Write a short list of everything you are currently anxious about regarding this. All of it — relapse at a wedding next summer, whether you will ever be normal, what happens if you tell your wife, whether you have ruined your kids.

Then go through and mark each one **T** for today or **L** for later.

Everything marked L — draw a line through it, and say out loud: *"That is not today's bread."*

It will come back. Do it again when it does. That is the practice.

Then ask God for exactly one day's worth. Nothing more.

## Today's Prayer

Father,

I have been trying to carry the rest of my life this morning.

Every future version of this, every occasion I will have to get through, every year stretching out — I have been holding all of it at once and then wondering why I cannot stand up.

You taught Your disciples to ask for today's bread. Just today's.

So that is what I am asking for.

Enough for today. Not for the wedding next year. Not for Christmas. Today.

And if today is too big, enough for this hour.

I will come back tomorrow and ask again. I understand that is how this works.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: What is one responsibility you could take on that would notice your absence?
devotional_text:
Idleness is not restful for somebody in your position. It is dangerous.

That is not a moral statement about laziness. It is an observation about what happens in an unstructured afternoon when you have nothing that needs you.

Day 34 said fill the house. Today is about one specific room in it: **work**.

# The Verse

> "And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men." (Colossians 3:23)

That is written to slaves in a Roman household — people whose work was genuinely menial and genuinely unchosen.

And Paul tells them their work has an audience they had not considered.

**As for the Lord.**

Which means there is no such thing, in Paul's mind, as work too ordinary to matter.

## Why This Is In A Study About Addiction

Three reasons, and they are all practical.

**1. Structure.** An hour that is accounted for is an hour that is much harder to lose. The dangerous hours are almost always the unaccounted ones.

**2. Being needed.** One of the quietest damages this does is making you feel useless. Somewhere in here you stopped believing you were any good to anybody. Work that depends on you contradicts that daily, without anybody having to give you a pep talk.

**3. Dignity.** Doing something well, with your hands or your mind, and seeing it finished — that gives a person something back that this thing has been stripping for years.

## "Whatever You Do"

This is not about having a prestigious job.

It is about having something that:

* 🕐 Happens at a set time
* 👀 Somebody notices if you do not do it
* ✅ Can be done well or badly, and you can tell the difference
* 🤲 Serves somebody other than you

A shift. A class. A responsibility at church. Fixing something for a neighbour. Caring for somebody. A volunteer slot. The garden.

**If you are out of work right now, this still applies**, and it matters more, not less. Unstructured months are where this does its worst work. Find something that expects you, even unpaid, even small, even three hours a week.

## A Warning

Work can also become the next addiction, and for some people it does.

The test is in the verse. *As for the Lord, and not for men.*

If you are working to prove something, to outrun the shame, to be so busy you never have to feel anything — that is not what Paul is describing. That is the same engine with a respectable badge on it.

The point is not to be exhausted. It is to be **occupied, useful, and accountable to a timetable.**

## What Comes With It

> "Knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance." (Colossians 3:24)

There is a reward, and it is not from the people watching.

That matters for you, because a lot of your work in this next year will go unnoticed. The ordinary Tuesday where nothing happened. The shift you turned up to when you felt terrible. Nobody will congratulate you.

It is seen. That is the promise.

## What To Watch For In Colossians 3:17-24

* 🗣️ Verse 17 — "whatever you do, in word or in deed"
* 🏠 The household instructions, and who they are addressed to
* 💓 "Work heartily" in verse 23 — literally, from the soul
* 👆 Who the real audience is
* 🎁 The reward in verse 24, and who it comes from

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have treated empty time as rest. For you, right now, a lot of it is exposure.

That will change in time. For this season, **an afternoon with nothing in it is a risk, and something that needs you is a defence.**

## Today's One Thing

**Take on one responsibility that would notice your absence.**

Not a big one. One.

* 📅 A regular slot somewhere — weekly, same day
* 🧑‍🔧 A job for somebody that they are now expecting
* 🏫 A class with a register
* ⛪ A task at church — setting up, clearing away, driving somebody
* 🧹 A standing thing at home that is yours and that people rely on

Commit to it today. Tell somebody you have committed to it, so it exists outside your own head.

Then do it on a day you do not feel like it. That is the whole exercise.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have a lot of hours that nobody is expecting anything from me in, and they are the hours where I come undone.

I have told myself that was rest. It is not rest. It is just space for this to move into.

Give me something to do that matters. Something somebody is counting on.

And help me do it as for You — not to prove anything, not to outrun how I feel, just honestly and well.

I have felt useless for a long time. I would like to be of some use to somebody again.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: What is one thing you could do at the same time every day for the next three weeks?
devotional_text:
On Day 5 we established that willpower is a battery.

Today is about the thing that works when the battery is flat.

# Daniel's Routine

Daniel is in his eighties, serving in a foreign government, when his rivals set a trap. They get the king to sign a law: anybody who prays to any god except the king for thirty days goes into the lions' den.

Here is what Daniel does.

> "When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before." (Daniel 6:10)

Four words at the end carry the whole story.

**"As he did before."**

He did not start praying because of the crisis. He did not pray harder, or longer, or differently.

He did exactly what he had been doing for decades, and the crisis found him already in the habit.

## Why This Matters More Than It Looks

Daniel did not have to decide, on the worst day of his career, whether he was going to pray.

The decision had been made thousands of times already. All he had to do was go upstairs at the usual hour.

**That is the whole principle: a habit decides in advance, so the moment does not have to.**

You have been relying on in-the-moment decisions, made by a tired person at the worst hour of the day, under pressure, while being argued with by something that knows all your weaknesses.

Daniel's method removes the decision from that moment entirely.

## Three Times A Day, Same Window

Notice the specifics.

Three times a day. Same room. Window open toward Jerusalem. Kneeling.

Time, place, posture, direction. All fixed.

That is not legalism; it is engineering. A routine with a fixed time and a fixed place survives a bad mood. A routine that depends on remembering and feeling like it does not.

## What To Make A Rhythm

For somebody in this fight, the candidates are obvious:

* 🌅 **The morning.** Same time, same chair, this study. Before the phone.
* 🕘 **The hour.** Day 32's plan, every night, same thing, until it is automatic.
* 📞 **The check-in.** Same day each week with the person from Day 28, whether or not you need it.
* 🛏️ **The shutdown.** Same bedtime, phone in another room, every night.
* 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 **The meeting.** Same night each week. You go when you are fine, which is why it holds when you are not.

**Go when you do not need it. That is what makes it there when you do.**

## And It Did Not Spare Him The Lions

Be honest about how the story goes.

Daniel's routine did not prevent the crisis. He still went into the den.

It did not stop the trouble. It made him the kind of man who walked through it without panicking and without compromising.

That is what a rhythm does. It does not guarantee an easy life. It builds somebody who is harder to knock over.

## The Honest Timescale

A habit is not formed in a week. It usually takes weeks of doing it badly, on days you do not want to, with no sense that anything is happening.

The early part feels pointless. Everybody quits in the early part.

**Do it when it is boring. Boring is the stage just before it becomes automatic.**

## What To Watch For In Daniel 6

* 📜 How the trap is designed in verses 4 to 9 — they could only get him on his faith
* 🪟 The open windows in verse 10 — he does not hide it, and he does not advertise it
* 🔁 "As he did before"
* 😴 The king who cannot sleep, in verse 18
* 🦁 Verse 23, and the reason given for why he is unhurt

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been trying to win this with decisions, made at the worst possible moment, by the most depleted version of you.

Daniel won it with a timetable.

**Build the rhythm while it is calm, so that when it is not calm there is nothing to decide.**

## Today's One Thing

**Pick one rhythm and fix all four variables.**

Write it down completely:

* ⏰ **When:** the exact time
* 📍 **Where:** the exact place
* 🔁 **What:** the exact thing
* 📆 **How often:** every day, or a named day each week

Then set the alarm now, with a label.

And commit to three weeks regardless of how it feels. You are not doing it for the feeling. You are building something that will be standing when the feeling is gone.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have been making this decision fresh every single night, at the time of day when I am least able to make it.

No wonder I keep losing.

Daniel had a time and a place and a window, and when the worst day came he just did what he always did.

Build something like that in me.

Help me keep it on the days when it feels pointless, which I think will be most of the early ones.

I am not asking to feel something. I am asking to become somebody who shows up.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: Look back over days 31-40. What have you actually put in place? Write the list.
devotional_text:
Forty days.

The last ten have been the practical ones — your body, your hour, your triggers, the empty house, your company, the wall, daily bread, work, rhythm.

Today closes that part by naming what guards it.

# The Instruction

> "In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God." (Philippians 4:6)

Three things in there, and the third is the one people skip.

**Prayer.** **Petition** — specific asking. And **with thanksgiving.**

That last one is not decoration. For somebody in this fight it is medicine, because the mind under this condition becomes extremely good at scanning for what is wrong and almost blind to what is not.

Gratitude is a deliberate correction to a bias you have developed.

## And Then The Promise

> "And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus." (Philippians 4:7)

**Guard.** It is a military word — a garrison posted around a city.

Notice what it guards: your **heart** and your **thoughts**. Exactly the two places where this fight is actually lost, as Days 24 and 25 established.

And notice what it does not promise. Not that you will understand. Not that the circumstances resolve. The peace *surpasses* understanding, which means it can be present while nothing makes sense.

## Then He Tells You Where To Point Your Mind

> "Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things." (Philippians 4:8)

That is Day 24 made concrete.

Not *stop thinking about the wrong thing* — we established the mind cannot do negatives. **Think about these things.** Direct it somewhere.

It is a list of destinations, not a list of prohibitions.

## And Then The Least Spiritual Verse In The Passage

> "The things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me: do these things, and the God of peace will be with you." (Philippians 4:9)

**Do these things.**

After all the talk of peace and thinking, Paul lands on practice.

Learned, received, heard, saw — and now *do*.

That is the right note to end the practical section on. Everything in the last ten days only works if it is done, repeatedly, mostly without feeling anything.

## Where You Actually Are

Be honest in both directions today.

Some of you have built real things in the last ten days. A filter, a bedtime, a meeting, a person who knows, an hour with something in it.

Some of you have read ten days of good ideas and implemented none of them, and you know it.

If that is you, **do not treat that as another failure to add to the pile.** Pick one. Today. The smallest one. A list of forty undone things becomes paralysis; one done thing becomes momentum.

## What Is Coming

The next ten days are the ones most studies leave out.

**Days 41-50: when you fall.**

Not if. We are going to deal with it honestly, because the difference between somebody who recovers and somebody who does not is very rarely whether they ever relapsed. It is what they did in the hour afterwards.

If you have already fallen during these forty days, that section is written for you. If you have not, read it anyway, before you need it.

## What To Watch For In Philippians 4:4-9

* 🙂 "Rejoice in the Lord always" in verse 4 — written from prison
* 🙏 The three parts of verse 6, especially the third
* 🛡️ The military word "guard" in verse 7
* 🎯 That verse 8 gives destinations rather than prohibitions
* 🔨 "Do these things" in verse 9

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have spent ten days building. Walls, rhythms, hours, people, defences.

All of it is guarded by something you cannot build: the peace of God, posted around your heart and your thoughts.

**You do the building. He does the garrison. Neither one replaces the other.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write the inventory.**

Go back through days 31 to 40 and list what you have actually put in place. Not what you intended. What exists.

Then, under it, list what you read and did not do.

Pick **one** from the second list and do it today.

And then, before you close this: write down three things you are thankful for about the last forty days. Three. Even if one of them is just *I am still reading this*.

That is the thanksgiving in verse 6, and it is not optional window dressing. It is the part that guards everything else.

## Today's Prayer

God,

Forty days.

I have built some things. I have let other things slide. You have watched all of it.

Thank You that I am still here. That is not nothing, and three months ago I would not have bet on it.

Guard what has been built. I know how quickly I can take it apart.

Put Your peace around my heart and my thoughts, because those are the two places where I keep losing this, and I cannot garrison them myself.

And in the next ten days, when we talk about falling — give me the honesty to read it without despair, and the humility to read it before I need it.

In Jesus' name, amen.
